To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
HlyA is a toxin that is delivered by erythrocyte membrane vesicles.
HlyA induces erythrocyte shedding of MVs that contain HlyA and phosphatidyl serine.
HlyA induces the secretion of MVs containing HlyA by a mechanism involving purinergic receptor stimulation, which is a new mechanism by which the toxin is eliminated from the erythrocyte membrane.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the mechanisms of action of the major virulence factors of E. coli, which are the alpha-hemolysin (a toxin) and the type I pili.
the study of HlyA, a toxin that is the main virulence factor of UPEC strains.
the elucidation of the mechanisms involved in the action of bacterial toxins, and in particular the mechanism of action, of HlyA.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
HlyA-MV is an important factor for the pathogenicity of UPEC.

the induction of microvesicles is one of the mechanisms by which UPEC strains can evade the immune system, and this is a new mechanism of pathogenicity of UPEC strains that should be taken into account in the development of new therapeutic strategies.
HlyA induces eryptosis and the delivery of MV by erythrocyte.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have shown that HlyA induces the formation of MVs that contain HlyA and that the release of these MVs is dependent on the activation of P2X7 receptors and the subsequent increment of intracellular Ca2+.
HlyA induces the delivery of MV containing toxin by erythrocyte and that this mechanism may be a protective mechanism on part of erythroctes that eliminates the toxin to prevent the spread infection.
we have demonstrated for the first time the induction of erythrocytic MVs by a sublytic toxin, and that the MVs contain the toxin and PS.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HlyA is eliminated by erythrocyte shedding MVs.
the secretion of MVs by HlyA-treated red blood cells might be considered a protective mechanism that removes the toxin to prevent the spread and severity of the infection.
the toxin is not only responsible for the hemolytic activity of UPEC, but it is also involved in the delivery of MV, which may be a defense mechanism against the spread of infection in patients.
